input.brief: a personal night diary that lives like a dark fairy tale photographed for real: misty forests, a figure in a cloak, candlelight, a castle in fog, aurora; every entry has a mood, the weather and a song; strangers leave notes

direction.name: The pinned poster
direction.idea: Something stays put while everything else changes. A title holds its place across the viewport and the images beneath it swap; the name is split to two opposite corners and the page passes between the halves; a single frame stays centred while its contents change. Every scroll step is a new cover of the same magazine. The idea suits subjects that are a series (a book of portraits, a line-up, a collection, a set of projects): the fixed element says what the series is, the changing element shows its members.
direction.composition: A sticky layer holds the fixed element for the height of two to three viewports: usually the title at 10–14vw across the middle or top of the screen, or two words pinned to the top-left and bottom-right corners. Under it, a stack of full-height panels scrolls by, each a single large photograph (portrait 4:5, centred, 40–50% of the viewport wide) with one line of caption at the same small size everywhere. The title sits above the images in the stacking order and uses `mix-blend-mode: difference` or a solid colour that reads on every panel. When the pinned run ends, the page releases into ordinary flowing sections with a narrow measure. Build with `position: sticky`; never hijack the scroll.
direction.typography: The pinned title is the only large type on the page. Captions and body share one small size (15–17px). Tight tracking and solid weight so the title reads over photographs.
direction.colour: One strong title colour against a pale or dark ground. Each panel may take its own flat ground colour sampled from its photograph.
direction.imagery: A series of photographs with the same crop ratio and the same framing (all portraits, all objects, all rooms), so that swapping them reads as one image changing. Five to eight in the pinned run.
direction.richness: Repetition with change. The fixed title makes each new photograph feel like an event, so the photographs must be good and consistent.
direction.pitfalls: If the title is not legible over every panel, the idea fails: test each one. Keep the pinned run under six viewports or it feels like a trap. On a phone the title shrinks to 16–18vw and stays pinned at the top; panels become full-width. A pin longer than three screens, or one where the screens under it are nearly empty, read in blind tests as a stuck page. Every screen under the pin needs its own content, and nothing may pass over the pinned words.

hero.name: Sentence split by a frame
hero.blueprint: A white or pale ground. One short sentence is broken in two and pushed to the edges: the first half flush to the 32px left margin, the second half flush to the right margin, both on the vertical centre line at clamp(40px, 3.6vw, 60px), medium weight. Between them, dead centre on columns 5–8, sits one media frame: 35% of the viewport wide, 16:9, corners 4px, holding a photograph or a working fragment of the product. The frame belongs to a vertical reel: the bottom 60px of the previous frame shows at the top edge of the viewport and the top 60px of the next at the bottom edge, same width, 24px gaps, so the centre column reads as a strip passing through the sentence. The stage is sticky; the reel advances three or four steps while the two halves of the sentence hold their place. Wordmark top-left; three text links and the single action as a small solid button top-right, all at 15px. Bottom-left on columns 1–4: one supporting sentence at 18px, its last line 32px above the bottom edge. The other corners stay empty.
hero.mobile: The halves stack: the first half of the sentence at 9vw flush left under the wordmark, then the frame at full width minus 16px margins and 4:3, then the second half flush right at 9vw. The neighbouring frames show as 28px slivers above and below. The supporting sentence and the action button follow at 16px. The links collapse to one word.
hero.headline: One sentence of four to six words split into two halves of up to about 14 characters each; the frame between them shows what it is about.

type.note: A compact, warm grotesk set heavy with letters almost touching; small text stays in the same family at semibold. Suits music, events and culture pages where the type is the image.

palette.name: Blush and aubergine
palette.note: Blush pink and dark aubergine alternate as full fields and serve as each other's text colour, in roughly equal shares. There is no third colour: the button is a solid block of whichever of the two is not the ground.

motion.name: Pinned story
motion.description: One element holds its place with `position: sticky` (a title, a frame, a product fragment) while the items that belong to it scroll past or swap inside it. The page's ordinary scrolling does the work; nothing is hijacked. Hold it for about one screen per step and three screens at most, two held stages per page at most, with a line of text on every held screen. Recipe: 'Pinned story' in references/motion.md.

sections.name: Pinned sentence, photographs pass
sections.blueprint: A wrapper 300svh tall. Inside it a `position: sticky; top: 0` layer of 100svh holds one sentence of 8–14 words, centred, three lines at clamp(36px, 4.6vw, 68px), leading 1.1, in a block 62% of the viewport wide. The sentence is a paragraph, not a heading; it is white with `mix-blend-mode: difference` (or a solid ink that reads over every photograph) and has a higher `z-index` than the images. Behind it, three photographs sit in normal flow at different sizes and sides and scroll past the fixed sentence: a 4:5 portrait 24vw wide with its left edge at 6vw; 70svh lower a 16:10 landscape 38vw wide touching the right margin; 70svh lower a 1:1 frame 18vw wide starting at 30vw. Each crosses the sentence once. When the wrapper ends, the sentence releases and scrolls away with the last photograph. No scroll hijacking.
sections.mobile: Wrapper 260svh. The sentence pins at 40% of the screen height at 8.4vw, four or five lines, with 20px margins. Photographs alternate: 64% wide on the left margin, 78% wide on the right margin, then 52% on the left, with 50svh between them.

sections.name: Sticky photograph, active list
sections.blueprint: Two columns. The left, columns 1–5, is `position: sticky; top: 12vh` and holds one photograph or object at 4:5, 34vw wide, unframed on the ground. The right, columns 7–11, holds a vertical list of five to nine names (treatments, rooms, courses, services) at clamp(20px, 1.6vw, 24px), each row 58px tall with the name at the left and a price or duration right-aligned at 15px in the soft ink. The active row is full ink; the others rest at 40% opacity. Hovering, focusing or scrolling a row to the middle of the viewport makes it active, crossfades the left photograph to that item's image over 300ms, and opens a three-line description at 15px, 34ch wide, directly under the name, pushing later rows down. A heading of two or three words at clamp(32px, 3.4vw, 48px) sits above the list, aligned to its left edge, 48px above the first row.
sections.mobile: The photograph becomes a 4:3 band pinned to the top of the screen at 38svh while the list scrolls beneath it; the heading sits above the first row. Rows are 56px tall and the description opens on tap. The image changes with the row nearest the band.

sections.name: One frame, contents change
sections.blueprint: Instead of many pictures side by side, one frame stays in place and its contents change. The frame is small and exact: 300px square on a quiet page, or up to 40vw at 4:5 on an object-led one, centred or sitting on the text column's left edge, with at least 20vh of empty ground above and below. Five to seven photographs are stacked inside it with `position: absolute` and crossfade in turn (opacity over 600ms, each held for 2.4 seconds, via CSS keyframes with staggered delays). All are shot or cropped alike: same scale, same light direction, the subject at the same position, so only the subject seems to change. On a flat ground use `mix-blend-mode: multiply` so studio backgrounds vanish. One caption line at 14px sits 16px below the frame and changes with the image. No arrows and no counter. On a motif-led page the frame takes the motif's shape through `clip-path`.
sections.mobile: The frame is 72vw wide, centred, in a section 70svh tall. The crossfade continues on its own; tapping the frame advances to the next image at once. The caption sits beneath, centred, at 14px. When reduced motion is requested the first image holds and tapping still advances.

sections.name: The email as display type
sections.blueprint: The section is 100svh in the inverse of the page's colours. A single email address is set as one line of display type spanning the content width: the font-size is fitted so the address runs from margin to margin (about 7–9vw for 20 characters; break after the @ onto two lines if it is longer than 26), light or regular weight, tight tracking, sitting on a baseline 12vh above the bottom edge. It is a `mailto:` link; on hover the whole line takes the accent ink. In the top-left corner, a sentence of up to 12 words at 20–22px says what to write about. In the two bottom corners at 14px: phone and city at the left, two or three social links at the right. No heading and no form. For a pinned ending, make the section `position: sticky; bottom: 0` beneath the page so the previous section lifts off it.
sections.mobile: The address breaks after the @ onto two lines at 11.5vw, left-aligned, sitting at 55% of an 86svh screen. The sentence sits at the top-left at 18px. Phone, city and social links stack at the bottom-left at 15px with 12px between them.

sections.name: Photograph half, menu half
sections.blueprint: A split footer one viewport tall. The left half is a single photograph filling columns 1–6 edge to edge, cropped hard by the left and bottom viewport edges: a close crop of the page's main subject, larger than it appeared anywhere above. The right half, on a flat field, is the site's menu set large: five or six section names stacked as links at about 2.6vw bold, 28px apart, starting at column 8 and 80px from the top. Rows are separated by space only; on hover a row's label shifts right by 12px and the others drop to the softer ink. Under the menu, 64px lower, two short blocks at 15px side by side: contact and social. The legal line runs along the very bottom of the right half at 12px. The wordmark sits small at the top of the right half, on the menu's left edge.
sections.mobile: The photograph leads at full width and 50svh, cropped tight. The menu follows on the flat field at 8vw per item with 20px between items, then contact and social stacked at 15px, then the legal line at 12px. The wordmark sits small above the menu.

references.name: City of Angels
references.idea: A fixed poster: the book title stays pinned across the viewport while portraits and press quotes swap underneath it, so every scroll step is a new cover.
references.hero: Pale icy-blue page. The title runs as one line of extra-bold uppercase grotesk at 10vw, centred, spanning about 82% of the width in saturated cyan, 120px from the top. A single portrait photograph, 37% of the viewport wide and nearly full height, is centred beneath; the title crosses over its upper quarter, so the middle letters sit on the image. The author name sits top-centre in small bold caps, a two-bar menu icon top-right. Bottom-left, a 13-line bold paragraph in a narrow 340px column; bottom-right, a solid black five-point star about 70px wide.
references.type: ABC Diatype throughout: weight 800 uppercase for the 144px title, bold copy around 20-24px with leading near 1.0; Founders Grotesk Mono in tiny caps for quote attributions. Two sizes plus a label. The final frame catches title letters slanting to oblique.
references.colour: #e4f8fd #06aeef #0a0a0a #c8b59d — The page colour is a pale tint of the title's cyan; cyan appears only on the title, the opening words and quotation marks. Text and star are black. The digest records one solid cyan section.
references.imagery: Full-length street-style portraits, all vertical at about 2:3, saturated natural light, subject standing centre. One image at a time, square corners, centred on the page with the title overprinting it.
references.layout: One pinned composition repeated for seven screens: central image column, fixed title, and a single text block that alternates between the left and right gutters and shifts height each step. Margins about 46px; nothing else on screen.

sections.description: Each scroll step keeps the pinned title and swaps the central portrait. One press quote sits in a column 180-340px wide in an outer gutter, alternating right, left, right, and placed at a different height each time (upper, middle, lower). Quotes are bold black with tight leading and cyan quotation marks; the source follows in tiny underlined or mono caps. The black star stays bottom-right and is caught at different rotation angles.

Not captured in the shots, but the digest records four stacked, centred, uppercase links at 144px (10vw) in the same extra-bold grotesk, plus a solid cyan section: navigation reuses the title's exact type size, one link per line, so the menu is another poster rather than a small list.

steal: Pin one giant title across the viewport and let a single centred image change beneath it, with the type overprinting the photo's top quarter.
Use a pale tint of the accent colour as the page background so the saturated title and the background read as one hue.
Give each scroll step one text block and move it between left and right gutters at varying heights instead of stacking sections.

references.name: Glitch&Grit
references.idea: Every screen is one project: two half-width footage columns with the project name stacked dead centre across their seam in a single flat pastel that changes per project.
references.hero: Black viewport split down its vertical centre. The left half holds a huge flat grey flower silhouette bleeding off the left and bottom edges; the right half is black with a few tiny video thumbnails drifting through. Dead centre, straddling the split, sits a two-line uppercase title in mint green, about 11vw per line, lines almost touching, spanning roughly 70% of the width. Two tiny category lines sit directly above it and a tiny 'view full project' link directly below, all in the same green. Navigation is six small bold white words pinned to the frame: three links across the top edge, the three-part studio name across the bottom edge.
references.type: Elza only, weight 900, uppercase, tracking -0.05em so letters nearly collide, line-height under 1. Just two sizes exist: roughly 158px project titles and 12px bold caps for nav, tags and links, a 13:1 jump with nothing in between.
references.colour: #000000 #999999 #9ae187 #93f1f7 #dcc8ff #fbb060 — Black ground and dark-graded footage. The only flat colour is the title lock-up, which takes a new candy pastel per project: mint, cyan, lilac, cornflower, lemon, orange.
references.imagery: Client film footage in two half-width columns per screen, cropped tight, graded dark, square edges, the two columns vertically offset against each other. One flat grey cut-out flower shape opens the sequence.
references.layout: No margins or containers. Each project is a full viewport cut into two equal media columns with one centred title lock-up. Fixed corner navigation frames every screen; fourteen screens repeat the same slide with different footage and title colour.

sections.description: Each scroll stop is a project slide. Two half-width media columns fill the viewport edge to edge and travel vertically at different offsets, so their top and bottom seams never align. Centred over the join: a two-line 11vw uppercase title in one flat pastel, with two or three 12px tag lines stacked above and a 12px 'view full project' or 'coming soon' line beneath. Title colour changes on every slide; nothing else does.

There is no footer block. The last screen is simply another project slide, and the studio name fixed along the bottom edge in three pieces (first word bottom-left, ampersand bottom-centre, last word bottom-right) does the footer's job on every screen, mirroring the three nav words fixed along the top edge at the same size and weight.

steal: Break the studio name into three words pinned bottom-left, bottom-centre and bottom-right, mirroring three nav links across the top, so the viewport frame itself is the logo.
Give each project slide one flat pastel used only for its title and tags, so a colour change is the sole signal that the project changed.
Split the viewport into two media columns that scroll at different offsets and set the title across the seam so the type stitches the halves together.
references.media: Media fills the whole first screen: a flat grey cut-out flower on the left half and a scatter of small thumbnails on the right that grows into a collage round the title. Then video is the main medium: each project is two full 720x900 half panes of muted, looping footage moving in opposite directions, with the title straddling the seam; about 24 pieces of footage or illustration across twelve projects.
references.motion: After a 10.7s load the thumbnail grid fills the right half by 1.2s and scales into a cluster by 4.5s, and Lenis then runs 40 scrubbed ScrollTriggers on empty 855px track divs: per project the left pane and half-title travel one way and the right ones the other (titles ±270px, panes ±180px), lining up only at the centre, and the scroll resets for an endless loop. Panes grow from an edge by scaleY over 0.5s, tags slide on y over 0.5s power2, and there is no reduced-motion rule.

references.name: Glide Typeface
references.idea: The page background is one grainy sky that passes from midday blue through sunset pink to a starry night as you scroll down the résumé.
references.hero: Full-viewport grainy gradient: saturated sky blue at the top fading through pale pink to warm amber at bottom-left, with soft diagonal cloud streaks. A translucent white pill navigation bar about 62% of the viewport wide floats centred at the top, name at its left and five links at its right. The name is centred at about 33% height in a tight italic display serif at 6.7vw on one line. Beneath it: a two-line sans introduction at roughly 2vw, a white pill button with a blue dot and blue label, then an underlined text link. The lower 35% of the screen is empty gradient.
references.type: editorialOld italic at 96px with -0.02em tracking for the name and section headings, and upright in a narrow cut for one large pull statement; Inter 18px for body, nav and buttons. About a 5:1 jump from display to body. Sentence case, four sizes.
references.colour: #3d9be9 #e8d9d7 #f3d5b8 #6f86d6 #e7b9c4 #1f4a5a — The gradient is the palette: blue to peach, periwinkle with white streaks, pink dusk, then deep teal night. Text flips from near-black to white as it darkens; cobalt is the accent.
references.imagery: No photographs. A full-bleed blurred sky gradient with diagonal cloud streaks and a visible film-grain overlay runs behind the entire page; small white star dots appear in the final night section.
references.layout: One narrow centred column, 45-60% wide, over a continuous background with no section boundaries or colour blocks. Blocks alternate between centred headings with pill buttons and left-aligned text. Experience is a left-rail timeline with glass cards; the footer is a five-column link list.

sections.description: A four-line statement in large upright serif at about 3.5vw, left-aligned inside the centred column, white over the periwinkle part of the sky. It is caught mid-reveal: the first words are fully opaque, the next few half-transparent, the rest at roughly 15% opacity, so the whole paragraph shape is visible before it fills in. Nothing else shares the viewport.

Vertical career timeline. A thin line at the far left of the column carries white-ringed blue dots, each paired with a date range in serif at about 1.6vw. To the right of each dot, a wide frosted-glass card with a 1px light border and rounded corners holds the company name in italic serif, the role in smaller italic, and one line of sans description. Cards are spaced about 150px apart over the pink dusk gradient.

Night sky in deep teal, lightening toward the bottom and scattered with tiny white star dots. A centred italic heading, a three-line centred paragraph and a pale pill button occupy the upper half. Below a faint hairline, five columns of small white links with bold column titles; the first column holds the name and location.

steal: Tie one long background gradient to page position so the palette tells time: day at the hero, dusk mid-page, night with stars at the footer, flipping text from dark to light on the way.
Lay visible grain over a blurred gradient with diagonal streaks so it reads as photographed sky rather than a CSS gradient.
Reveal a large statement word by word on scroll while keeping upcoming words at about 15% opacity, so the paragraph's full shape is present from the start.
